newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - May 29.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - May 29.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Thursday:

* Millions of Indonesians flocked to the polls on Thursday in national and local elections through the sprawling archipelago of more than 17,500 islands. Polls open from 8 a.m. to 2 p.m. (0100-0700 GMT).
* On Wednesday, the Dow Jones industrial average lost 26.18 points to close at 7,357.23, a day after jumping 38 points to a record 7,383.41 as investors took profits after the previous day's rally.
* The central bank clearing house will be closed for the election day, which brokers said would affect exchange transactions.

* On Wednesday, the Jakarta composite index rose 3.65 points to close at 672.50 points with sustained buying interest in blue chips despite election eve jitters and a hoax bomb threat against the Japanese embassy, brokers said.
* On Thursday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,440.00/1.00 at 0150 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,438.50/40.50.
* Toll road operator Citra Marga Nusaphala on market talks that its net profit in the first quarter would be about 30 billion rupiah, higher than its net profit in the same period last year.

* Heavyweight telecommunications firm PT Telkom ahead of its announcement of first quarter results on Friday. Also following reports that Telkom subsidiary cellular operator Telkomsel planned to float its shares later this year.
* Blue chip telecommunications firm PT Indonesian Satelite (Indosat) on a news report that it had denied rumours of a secondary offering.
* Car maker after it announced 1997 first quarter net profit of 119.83 billion rupiah, up from 73.46 billion rupiah in the same period last year.
* Cigarette stocks such as Sampoerna and Gudang Garam on reports the government was planning to issue regulations banning smoking in certain public places.
* Sampoerna after it announced that it posted a net profit at 99.56 billion rupiah, compared with 84.21 billion rupiah in the same period in 1996.
* Retailer Multipolar following its announcement of 1997 first quarter net profit of 20.1 billion rupiah, up 927 percent from the same period last year.
* Surabaya-based property firm Mas Murni Indonesia on revived market talk that the firm was a target for a take-over.
